full_judgment: 12. Introducing certain broad themes in his opening arguments, the learned Deputy Attorney General Mr Bhishmadev Chakrabortty has submitted that the case against the condemned prisoners has been proven based on circumstantial evidence. Badshah's testimony as PW 5 and the confessional statement of Moksed buttressed firmly by corroborating statements of various prosecution witnesses. Mr Chakrabrtty terms Moksed's confessional statement as reliable given that it was made merely a day after his arrest and that during the trial he did not draw attention to any wrongful extraction of his confession even though he had opportunity to do so for example, in the course of his examination under section 342 of the code. The resultant presumption against an irregular extraction of Moksed's confession is further fortified. it is submitted from the express satisfaction of the recording Magistrate that the section 164-confession was made voluntarily by Moksed who otherwise appeared to be in overall good physical condition. The learned DAG has also taken care to draw this Court's attention to the section 342 examinations of the other condemned Prisoner Tutul who was duly informed of Moksed having implicated Tutul in the confessional statement. but in response to which there is nothing on record to show that Tutul uttered anything to dispute, contradict or in any other way distance himself from any such assertion or attestation by Moksed.
